movement_source: row 'Cash earnings', column FY24 -> column FY25
headline: NAB's cash earnings decreased by $11 million to $7,091 million in FY25 (FY24: $7,102 million). Total operating income increased by $644 million (3.8%) driven by higher NII and other operating income. Operating expenses rose significantly by $435 million (4.6%), including $130 million of notable payroll review and remediation costs. Credit impairment charges were flat at $833 million. Income tax expense increased by $27 million. The net result was a slight decline in core profit.

drivers.narrative: Increased by $644 million (3.8%). Driven by volume growth of $22.5 billion (2.3%) in average interest earning assets and a 3 bps margin expansion. Includes a $74 million decrease from economic hedges, offset in other operating income.
Decreased by $67 million (1.9%). Net fees fell $132 million; trading rose $33 million; other income rose $32 million. A $74 million hedge movement reducing NII was fully offset here.
Underlying operating expenses increased by $305 million (3.2%), excluding notable items. Personnel costs rose $170 million, technology $71 million, general $52 million, and occupancy $12 million.
Notable increase of $130 million for payroll review and remediation costs ($101 million in personnel, $29 million in general expenses).
No change. Cash credit impairment charge remained flat at $833 million in both periods.
Tax expense increased by $27 million (0.9%) due to higher pre-tax earnings and a 10 bps rise in the effective tax rate to 29.6%.

limitations: Capped at 80: credit_impairment_charge +0 $m. The records these claims cite do not state those numbers, so each one is arithmetic over the evidence rather than a figure read from it.
Expenses are claimed on the underlying/notable split; the bank equally publishes the combined headline framing, so both claims are capped at 80.
Failed check: drivers_reconcile (drivers +115.0 + residual +0.0 != delta -11.0, tol 1.0)

Capped at 80: nii +644 $m, other_operating_income -67 $m, tax_and_other -27 $m. drivers_reconcile failed, so the parts and the whole disagree. That proves one of these claims is wrong without saying which, so none of them may claim near-certainty.

evidence_records.quote: Group cash earnings reconciliation to statutory net profit

NAB uses cash earnings (rather than statutory net profit attributable to owners of the Company) for its internal management reporting purposes and considers it a better reflection of the Group’s underlying performance.

Cash earnings is not a statutory financial measure and is not presented in accordance with Australian Accounting Standards nor audited or reviewed in accordance with Australian Auditing Standards. Cash earnings is calculated by excluding discontinued operations and certain other items which are included within the statutory net profit attributable to owners of the Company.
